NXS TCS Article — Chapter Analysis

How do the keypaper concepts link across the TCA/Nexus key-sets?

Author

Rainer M. Krug

Published

August 25, 2026

This report examines how the keypaper concepts (the TCA/Nexus definitions) link to one another across the two key-sets — especially the association between TCA Approaches and TCA Actions — and how coherent the keypaper set itself is. It builds toward the combined Approach × Action heatmap at the end.

The heavier corpus-wide analyses (chapter alignment, score distributions, work-type and citation breakdowns) and the cited-literature-embedding “Stage 3” signal have been removed: they depend on the full-corpus embeddings, which are no longer computed in this pruned pipeline.

Keyset linkage

How do the concept definitions link to one another across the two key-sets (the worksheet groups TCA_Approaches_3_2 and TCA_Actions_Ch5)? The association of interest is TCA Approaches with TCA Actions, shown below as Sankeys and heatmaps. Two complementary similarity signals drive it:

  • Stage 1 — definition-text similarity (embeddings): cosine similarity between the keypaper definition embeddings (title_abstract, BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5, 1024-dim; title and abstract are concatenated directly, as BGE has no [SEP] convention). Two definitions link if their wording/concepts are close.
  • Stage 2 — cited-literature overlap (no embeddings): two definitions link if they cite the same works — Jaccard overlap (Jaccard 1912) of the resolved cited-work sets.

Both measures are symmetric: the association between an Approach and an Action carries no direction, so the Sankeys’ left-to-right arrangement is a layout convention, not a claim about influence.

Jaccard, P. (1912). The distribution of the flora in the alpine zone. New Phytologist, 11(2), 37–50. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-8137.1912.tb05611.x (the “coefficient of community”, defined on p. 39: species common to both / total species in both).

TCA Approaches ↔︎ TCA Actions Ch5

TCA Approaches with TCA Actions: for each Approach, its most-similar Actions under each signal stage.

The Sankeys above only show each Approach’s top matches; the heatmaps below show every Approach × Action pair for both signals. Black borders mark cells in the top 5% of all concept-definition pairs for that measure. This is a rank threshold, not a statistical test: about 5% of any set of pairs clears it by construction, there is no null model of “no association”, and no correction is applied for the 264 simultaneous comparisons. Treat a border as “unusually high for this measure”, not as evidence against chance.

Combined (Stage 1 + Stage 2, equal weight)

Each cell blends Stage 1 and Stage 2 as equal-weight indicators — each stage’s value expressed as a percentile rank against the distribution of that measure over all ordered pairs of concept definitions, then averaged, so neither measure’s raw scale dominates.

Show code 
tar_read(viz_pair_heatmap_appr_act_combined_fig)

*Approach × Action, combined Stage 1 + Stage 2 (equal-weight mean percentile). Center number (large) = the combined score; bottom-left (small) = Stage 1 definition-text cosine similarity; bottom-right (small) = Stage 2 cited-literature Jaccard overlap, multiplied by 10 so it is legible (the raw values run 0–0.09, which would print as “0.00” for most cells); the scaling is display-only and does not affect the colour, the bold rule or the border. Bold marks a value in the top 5% of all concept-definition pairs for its own measure; the center number is bold whenever either component is. Border style (solid = both stages, dashed = one stage only) is keyed in the figure’s own “Individual-stage link” legend. Emphasis follows the unrounded value, so two cells printing the same rounded number can differ.

Fill colour and border answer two different questions, and they need not agree. The fill tracks the center number — how unusual this pair is — on ColorBrewer’s colour-blind-safe RdBu palette, running from 0 to 1. Each stage’s value is ranked against all pairs of concept definitions, including Action–Action and Approach–Approach pairs, and the two ranks are averaged. Because within-keyset pairs are systematically more similar than Approach × Action pairs, and because most pairs share no citations at all, the typical Approach × Action cell scores about 0.43–0.45 rather than 0.5 — so the map reads predominantly blue. Read the colour as a relative ranking across the whole figure, not as an absolute statement that a given pair is “below typical”.

The border answers instead whether an individual stage falls in the top 5% for its own measure, and the small bottom numbers are bold on the same test. A cell can therefore be distinctly red yet carry no border (42 cells here), or carry a border while sitting near white: the colour ranks the blended score, the border and bold marks flag the individual stages.

Three limitations to keep in mind when reading Stage 2. First, it is close to binary rather than graded: pairs sharing no citations all sit at the same rank (0.39), and the smallest non-zero overlap already jumps to 0.77. Second, Jaccard is normalised by reference-list size, so it measures proportional rather than absolute overlap — a pair sharing one reference out of few can outrank a pair sharing two out of many, and indeed does so here. Third, and consequently, definitions with longer reference lists tend to look better connected (r = 0.51 between citation count and mean combined score across Actions). The “Jaccard overlap” is Jaccard’s coefficient of community (Jaccard 1912, p. 39; species common to both / total species in both) — the term “Jaccard index” is a later name, not used in the original paper.*
